$comment: Coldline Task 2.7 public answer contract. Eight direct answers describe one controlled experiment: which approved parameter was tuned and to what, the deterministic Recall@K and p95 latency of both arms, how the deterministic metric and the cached judge evidence moved relative to each other, and the adoption decision. The automated checks re-measure the running system and compare every recorded value against that measurement; the decision is checked against the published adoption support policy in docs/student/task-2-7-contract.md.
title: Coldline Task 2.7 answers
description: One controlled retrieval experiment, recorded from benchmark output.

answers.description: The only top-level answer mapping accepted by the public verifier.

selected_parameter.description: Which approved retrieval parameter was tuned in config/student/retrieval.yaml. Exactly one may differ from config/retrieval-baseline.yaml.

parameter_value.description: The experimental value assigned to that parameter, exactly as it appears in config/student/retrieval.yaml. Bounded per parameter below: top_k is a whole number from 1 to 12, the fixed candidate pool each arm fetches before fusion; fusion_weight is a number from 0.0 to 1.0.

baseline_recall_at_k.description: Mean deterministic Recall@K of the baseline arm over the golden evaluation set, to three decimal places, from `poe benchmark`.

experiment_recall_at_k.description: Mean deterministic Recall@K of the experimental arm over the same golden evaluation set, to three decimal places, from `poe benchmark`.

baseline_latency_ms.description: The baseline arm's 95th-percentile query latency in milliseconds, from the p95 column of `poe benchmark`. Not the median and not seconds.

experiment_latency_ms.description: The experimental arm's 95th-percentile query latency in milliseconds, from the p95 column of `poe benchmark`.

agreement_classification.description: How the authoritative deterministic metric and the comparison-only cached judge relevance moved relative to each other: `agreement` when both moved the same way, `disagreement` when they moved in opposite directions, `mixed_or_no_change` when neither moved or only one did. From `poe compare`.

adoption_decision.description: Whether to retain the experimental configuration (`keep`) or restore the baseline (`revert`). Checked against the published adoption support policy: where the recorded evidence is one-sided, only the decision it points to is accepted; where the arms trade off or nothing moved, either decision is accepted.

allOf.$comment: top_k is a candidate count, bounded by the fixed candidate pool.
fusion_weight is the dense arm's share of reciprocal-rank fusion.
